target.title: fix(slack): guard matchesSlackDeliveryMetadataSignature against UTF-8/UTF-16 length mismatch
target.body:
## Summary

`matchesSlackDeliveryMetadataSignature` compared JS string `.length` (UTF-16 code units) before calling `timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(…))` (UTF-8 bytes). When the stored signature contains multi-byte characters, the UTF-16 length can match while the UTF-8 byte length differs, causing `timingSafeEqual` to throw `TypeError` and crash the message reconciliation loop. This patch compares Buffer byte lengths instead.

- Problem: `actual.length` (UTF-16) ≠ `Buffer.from(actual).length` (UTF-8) for multi-byte strings; the guard passes but `timingSafeEqual` receives unequal-length buffers → `TypeError`
- Solution: Convert to Buffers once, compare their byte lengths, reuse the same Buffers for `timingSafeEqual` — aligns with `raft/src/gateway.ts:100`
- What changed: `extensions/slack/src/send.ts` (length comparison), `extensions/slack/src/send.reconcile.test.ts` (multi-byte regression test)
- What did NOT change: Signature creation, metadata attachment, reconciliation loop logic, any other `timingSafeEqual` call site

## Change Type & Scope

### Change Type (multi-select)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor (must be explicitly requested by a maintainer)
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

### Scope (multi-select)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related to #105436
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Slack message send reconciliation uses `timingSafeEqual` to verify that a stored delivery metadata signature matches the expected HMAC. If a Slack app or user injects multi-byte Unicode characters into the signature field (e.g. emoji), `Buffer.from(actual)` produces more bytes than `actual.length` code units. When the string length coincidentally matches `expected.length` (a base64url HMAC), the length guard passes but `timingSafeEqual` throws `TypeError` because the two Buffers have different byte lengths.

This unhandled exception crashes the reconciliation loop, leaving sends in an unresolved state and potentially causing repeated retries or stuck delivery tracking.

## Review Contract

```text
Ref: #105436
Surface: extensions/slack — message send reconciliation

Bug: timingSafeEqual TypeError crashes reconciliation loop when stored
     signature contains multi-byte UTF-8 characters whose UTF-16 length
     matches expected
Cause: matchesSlackDeliveryMetadataSignature compared JS string .length
       (UTF-16 code units) before calling timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(…)),
       but Buffer.from defaults to UTF-8 encoding. Multi-byte chars produce
       different byte counts → TypeError. Confidence: clear
Provenance:
  introduced by: 7e0d530e07d (fix(slack): reconcile ambiguous sends before
                  replay #97480, 2026-07-05)
  made visible by: N/A (present from original introduction)
  Confidence: clear

Best fix: Yes. Comparing Buffer byte lengths directly aligns with the
          existing pattern in raft/src/gateway.ts:100 and removes the
          encoding mismatch at the source. No try-catch wrapper needed
          because the length guard now prevents the only error path.
Refactor: No
Proof: unit tests (17/17 pass including new multi-byte char regression test)
Risk: Low. expected is always ASCII (HMAC-SHA256 base64url), so the fix
      only changes behavior for actual values where UTF-16 length ≠ UTF-8
      byte length — exactly the bug scenario.
```

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: `matchesSlackDeliveryMetadataSignature` throws `TypeError` when `actual` contains multi-byte characters whose UTF-16 length matches `expected` but whose UTF-8 byte length differs.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19, branch `fix/slack-signature-utf8-105436`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Run the Slack reconciliation test suite including the new regression test
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/send.reconcile.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/send.reconcile.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/0668000999/OpenClaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
   Start at  23:18:38
   Duration  8.72s
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- All 16 existing reconciliation tests continue to pass — no regression
- New test "does not throw when the stored signature contains multi-byte UTF-8 characters" passes: the tampered emoji signature is rejected with `status: "unresolved"` instead of crashing with `TypeError`
- The fix matches the established pattern in `raft/src/gateway.ts:100` (`received.length === required.length && timingSafeEqual(received, required)` where both values are already Buffers)

**What was not tested**:

- Live Slack end-to-end roundtrip with actual multi-byte metadata injection (requires a real Slack workspace and a malicious/misconfigured app)
- Other `timingSafeEqual` call sites in the codebase (they use different patterns and are not affected)

### Verification Environment (supplementary)

- OS: Linux x86_64
- Runtime: Node 22.19
- Integration/channel: Slack (unit test, mocked client)

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: The `expected` value is always base64url (ASCII), so this fix only tightens the guard. If `expected` were ever changed to contain multi-byte characters, the comparison would still be correct (both sides use Buffer byte length).
- **Mitigation**: The fix reuses the same Buffer objects for both the length check and `timingSafeEqual`, so there is no second `Buffer.from` call that could produce a different result.
- **Compatibility impact**: None. This is a backward-compatible behavior change — strings that previously passed the guard and matched will still pass; strings that previously passed the guard but crashed will now correctly return `false`.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: Normal signature matching (existing tests), signature length mismatch (existing tests), multi-byte UTF-8 signature (new test), chunked text reconciliation (existing tests)
- **Edge cases checked**: Emoji character (U+1F600, 4-byte UTF-8) repeated to match original signature string length; empty/missing metadata; forged signatures with wrong part indices
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live Slack workspace end-to-end roundtrip

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Pending
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #105436 analysis → identified UTF-8/UTF-16 length mismatch in `matchesSlackDeliveryMetadataSignature` → compared against sibling patterns in `raft/gateway.ts`, `line/signature.ts`, `nextcloud-talk/signature.ts` → applied minimal Buffer-length fix → added regression test with emoji tampered signature

Related to #105436
